extracted.intended_audience: PTAB practitioners: petitioner and patent-owner counsel, patent prosecutors and litigators
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria the Patent Trial and Appeal Board applies when deciding whether to institute an inter partes review (IPR), including statutory thresholds (35 U.S.C. § 314), claim construction principles, burdens of proof/production, written description/priority-date analysis, and discretionary-denial considerations under § 325(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable likelihood standard for institution (35 U.S.C. § 314(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may institute review only upon a determination that 'there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least [one] of the claims challenged in the petition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory threshold the Board applies at institution. The Decision explains that, applying that standard to the preliminary record (e.g., uncontested mapping of claim limitations to a prior-art disclosure), the Board may institute review. Institution requires showing a reasonable likelihood as to at least one challenged claim; once met, the Board will institute on the petition's challenges (see SAS/PGS discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and regulatory basis to institute (35 U.S.C. § 314; 37 C.F.R. § 42.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has authority to determine whether to institute an inter partes review under 35 U.S.C. § 314 and implements institution under 37 C.F.R. § 42.4(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite statutory/regulatory authorities when assessing institution. The Decision frames the institution inquiry under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of ordinary skill in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the person of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA) for claim interpretation and validity analyses; petitioner proposed 'at least a graduate degree, such as a Masters or Ph.D., in a relevant discipline ... and between one and three years of experience in the research, design, development and/or testing of resist materials.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may adopt an uncontested POSITA definition for the preliminary record. Prior art disclosures can themselves reflect the appropriate skill level (Okajima v. Bourdeau). Use the agreed POSITA when construing terms and assessing whether prior art teaches/anticipates/obviously suggests claim limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard (plain and ordinary meaning / Phillips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim terms are construed 'in accordance with the ordinary and customary meaning of such claim as understood by one of ordinary skill in the art and the prosecution history pertaining to the patent' (37 C.F.R. § 42.100(b); Phillips v. AWH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms are generally given their plain and ordinary meaning within the context of the specification. The Board will expressly construe disputed terms only as necessary to resolve the controversy; if no express construction is necessary to resolve institution issues, the Board may decline to provide one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation (35 U.S.C. § 102) — mapping limitations with particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference anticipates a claim when it discloses each limitation of the challenged claim. Petitioner should map with particularity every limitation to disclosures in the reference (e.g., claim charts identifying where each limitation is disclosed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision cites Petitioner's detailed claim charts mapping each claim limitation to the '888 Publication' (including Example 4 disclosing a 20 nm coating) as sufficient on the preliminary record, particularly where Patent Owner does not meaningfully contest the mapping. Anticipation requires that every claim limitation is found in the single prior-art reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness (35 U.S.C. § 103) — asserted as separate grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. § 103 may be asserted as a ground of unpatentability in the petition (the Petition advances § 103 grounds in addition to § 102).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Decision institutes based on anticipation, § 103 grounds are recognized as valid bases for challenge and may be addressed at trial if institution occurs on those grounds as part of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of persuasion and burden of production for priority date disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner bears the ultimate burden of persuasion to prove unpatentability; Patent Owner bears the burden of production when relying on an earlier priority date to defeat a prior-art reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a Patent Owner asserts entitlement to an earlier effective filing date to avoid prior art, the Patent Owner must produce evidence to support that entitlement; the petitioner still retains the ultimate burden to prove unpatentability based on the applicable prior art and dates (citing Dynamic Drinkware).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written-description requirement for priority (Ariad test and related caselaw)
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim an earlier priority date, the specification of the earlier application must 'reasonably convey[] to those skilled in the art that the inventors had possession of the claimed subject matter' (Ariad). The level of detail required varies with the nature/scope of the claims and predictability of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 'four corners' inquiry (Ariad). Consider whether a broad disclosed range supports a narrower claimed range (RAI Strategic Holdings and Wertheim): ask whether the broad described range 'pertains to a different invention than the narrower (and subsumed) claimed range' and whether the disclosed range 'behaves any differently than the claimed range.' In unpredictable arts (e.g., chemical), higher detail is required. Absence of explicit endpoints and prosecution statements may weigh against priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prosecution statements and prosecution history on written-description/priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements made by the applicant/examiner during prosecution (e.g., distinguishing a prior-art coating of 35 nm from a claimed 30 nm) can bear on whether an earlier application conveys possession of the claimed range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision treats applicant statements to the Examiner (e.g., that '35 nm is not close enough' to 30 nm) as evidence that the broader range may not support the narrower claimed range and as supporting a preliminary finding against earlier priority. Whether prosecution-history estoppel applies is a separate issue; the Board may consider such statements in the written-description/priority inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of unpredictability of the art
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claimed subject matter lies in an unpredictable field (e.g., chemical arts), a higher level of disclosure/detail is required to satisfy written-description and enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision notes that 'the claimed invention is within the unpredictable chemical arts' and that unpredictability supports a preliminary finding that the prior application lacks sufficient detail to establish possession of the narrower claimed ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 325(d) discretionary-denial two-part test
rubrics_metrics.description: For discretionary denial under 35 U.S.C. § 325(d), the Board considers (1) whether the same or substantially the same issue was previously presented to the Examiner during prosecution and (2) whether the petitioner identifies a material error by the Examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Examiner previously considered the same issue but the petitioner identifies a material error (e.g., Examiner accepted priority without questioning), the Board may decline to exercise discretion to deny. The Decision found a material error where the Examiner failed to appreciate the prior-art status of the '888 Publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAS/PGS institution practice: all-or-none treatment of petition challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with SAS and PGS Geophysical, the Board's institution decision is a 'simple yes-or-no institution choice respecting a petition, embracing all challenges included in the petition.' The Board will not institute on fewer than all challenged claims or fewer than all challenges presented in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If institution is granted, it will apply to all claims and all grounds in the petition. The Decision institutes review of all challenged claims based on all grounds set forth in the Petition after finding the § 314(a) threshold satisfied for at least one ground/claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to map claim limitations with particularity (claim charts and evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner should support anticipation/obviousness arguments with detailed mapping (claim charts) showing where each claim limitation is found/disclosed in the asserted reference(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision relies on Petitioner's claim charts that 'map with particularity every limitation of the challenged claims to disclosures in the '888 Publication.' Where Patent Owner does not contest such mapping on the preliminary record, the Board may treat the mapping as sufficient for institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary nature of institution determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution decisions are preliminary; findings at institution are based on the preliminary record and are subject to change on the full trial record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision expressly notes that preliminary determinations (e.g., on priority/written description) are for the purpose of deciding institution and may change after a full trial record; parties are put on notice that the initial finding may be revisited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of issues not timely raised
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will deem waived any issue not raised by Patent Owner in a timely response to the Petition or as permitted later during trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner must raise issues in a timely preliminary response or risk waiver. The Decision warns parties about waiver consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on supplementation of petition grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner may not supplement the information supporting any ground advanced in the Petition except as permitted by Board rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision states that nothing in the institution order authorizes petitioner to supplement its petition in manners not permitted by Board rules; parties must follow PTAB practice for any additional evidence or new grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural effect of institution (commencement of trial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon institution under 35 U.S.C. § 314(c) and 37 C.F.R. § 42.4(b), an inter partes review of the challenged claims shall commence on the entry date of the Decision and notice is given of institution of trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision orders institution and sets the institution commencement; practitioners should note timing consequences and subsequent trial schedule and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may invite parties to streamline trial based on preliminary findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may provide optional guidance and invite parties to consider how preliminary determinations (e.g., on priority) might affect the sufficiency of petition showings and the scope of issues at trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Decision offers the parties an opportunity to address how preliminary priority determinations may impact asserted prior art and whether ultimate conclusions would change if priority is established differently at trial; this is a practice guidance to promote efficiency.
